“In the past I was miserable,
a widow without sons; bereft of friends and kinsmen, I lived alone.”
Without obtaining food from Bhattacoḷa,
she took her bowl and staff and went begging from family to family.
Burning with cold and heat,
I wandered for seven years; then,
having seen a bhikkhunī again, I...
To her who had obtained food and drink,
I approached and said:
“I am going forth into the homeless life.”
And out of compassion for me,
Paṭācārā ordained me; then,
having exhorted me, she—
He established me in the ultimate truth.
Having heard his words,
I carried out his instruction.
“The noble lady’s instruction was not in vain;
I am one of the threefold knowledge and free from taints.
… Thus spoke the Elder Nun Canda.
The Chapter of Five is finished.
